dimensions.assessment: Affects state governments administering TANF, low-income families receiving assistance and services, and the Department of Health and Human Services.
dimensions.evidence: A State to which a grant is made under section 403(a)(1) shall use the grant only to provide assistance or services to a family whose income is less than twice the poverty guidelines

dimensions.assessment: Restricts fund eligibility to lower-income thresholds, forces strict obligation/expenditure timelines, prohibits supplanting state funds, and applies federal payment integrity laws to states.
dimensions.evidence: The Payment Integrity Information Act of 2019 shall apply to a State with respect to the State program funded under this part in the same manner in which such Act applies to a Federal agency.

dimensions.assessment: Alters how billions in federal TANF block grant funds are obligated, spent, reserved (max 15%), and protected from supplanting state general revenues.
dimensions.evidence: a State to which funds are paid... for a fiscal year may reserve not more than 15 percent of the funds for future use

dimensions.assessment: Amends part A of title IV of the Social Security Act across multiple operational areas including eligibility, spending deadlines, non-supplantation certifications, and improper payments.
dimensions.evidence: To amend part A of title IV of the Social Security Act to target funds to low-income families, strengthen program integrity guardrails for State expenditure of funds, require measurement of improper payments

dimensions.assessment: Permanent programmatic changes effective beginning October 1, 2027, with ongoing 10-year reduction plans and regular reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this Act shall take effect on October 1, 2027.

importance_detail.rationale: Imposes strict new eligibility limits (under 200% of poverty guidelines), spending deadlines, maintenance of effort non-supplantation rules, and improper payment tracking under the Payment Integrity Information Act for the TANF block grant program.

other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 8872, Preventing Waste, Fraud, and Abuse in TANF Act

summary: H.R. 8872, the Preventing Waste, Fraud, and Abuse in TANF Act, places new restrictions and requirements on the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program. It sets an income limit for recipients, imposes deadlines for states to spend federal funds, prevents federal funds from replacing state funds, and requires states to track improper payments.

affected_groups.effect: Will face a uniform federal income threshold (under 200% of the federal poverty guidelines) to qualify for any TANF-funded assistance and services.

Must adhere to strict spending deadlines, prevent federal funds from supplanting state revenues, certify compliance regarding state funding, track improper payments, and report data under federal payment integrity laws.
Must submit a written report and 10-year plan to Congress to reduce or eliminate improper payments made by states.
affected_groups.group: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)

key_provisions: Establishes an upper income limit for all TANF-funded assistance and services, restricting them to families with incomes under 200 percent of the federal poverty guidelines.
Requires states to obligate TANF funds by the end of the fiscal year after they are paid, and to spend them by the end of the second fiscal year after payment.
Allows states to reserve a limited amount of TANF funds, up to 15 percent per year with a cap of 50 percent of the prior year's grant, for future use.
Prohibits states from using federal TANF funds to replace state and local funding for programs.
Requires states to track and report on improper payments and applies the Payment Integrity Information Act of 2019 to state TANF programs.
Directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to submit a plan to Congress within one year to eliminate improper TANF payments within 10 years.
missing_information: Exact financial estimates or costs associated with implementing the payment integrity tracking and reporting.
Specific details on penalties for states that fail to meet the new spending deadlines or improper payment reduction goals.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 8872, the Preventing Waste, Fraud, and Abuse in TANF Act, places new restrictions and requirements on the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program. It sets an income limit for recipients, imposes deadlines for states to spend federal funds, prevents federal funds from replacing state funds, and requires states to track improper payments.
summary_detail.significance: The bill changes federal oversight of the TANF program by tightening eligibility rules, imposing strict spending timelines on states, banning the replacement of state funds with federal dollars, and introducing formal measurements for improper payments.
